newsitem.title: USA: Moler top U.S. energy job pick -White House source.
newsitem.headline: Moler top U.S. energy job pick -White House source.

text.p: U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission chairwoman Elizabeth Moler is the top choice for filling the job of energy secretary, a White House official said Thursday.
"She is the leading candidate as far as I can tell," said the official, who asked not to be named.
"Betsy Moler represents the kind of consensus, confirmable candidate that no one is going to be outwardly uncomfortable with," he said.
President Clinton is expected to name his choice Friday for the energy slot and other cabinet positions.

The White House official said while everyone considered Moler to be a "competent, experienced" candidate, advocates of energy efficiency and renewable energy sources had questioned how committed she would be to their cause.

"The test for her will be whether she can demonstrate a commitment to the sorts of energy policies and environmental concerns associated with energy that have been part of this administration's attempt to balance traditional fossil and nuclear missions of the department with those of energy efficiency and renewables," he said.
Renewable and efficiency groups said Thursday they were still holding out for Nebraska Governor Benjamin Nelson, who founded the Governors' Ethanol Coalition, but were not opposed to Moler.
"She is universally respected," said David Nemtzow, president of the Alliance to Save Energy.

Senate Energy Committee chairman Frank Murkowski of Alaska said he would grill any nominee about the Clinton administration's plans to find a way to take spent nuclear fuel away from commercial power plants in 1998, as required under law.

"They should do their part by sending us a qualified nominee who can competently address nuclear waste issues and defend DOE (Energy Department) control of our weapons programs," Murkowski said in a statement Thursday.
